title: Organiser guide
text: Set up, run and finish a tournament without technical knowledge.

title: Organiser guide · Organiser guide
text: # Organiser guide  J3 runs a whole tournament from one place. This guide uses plain language and assumes no technical experience. Start with the demo: it is seeded with two clubs, officials, fighters, fights, kata scores and medals so you can click around before creating your own event.

title: Organiser guide · Before you start
text: Have these ready:  - the event name, dates and venue; - your logo and banner images (PNG, JPG, WEBP or SVG); - the clubs you expect and a rough number of fighters; - the age, weight, height and belt ranges you want to offer; - which disciplines you are running (fighting, ground, randori, kata and so on).  You do not need to know rules or point values from memory. J3 offers sensible defaults for ev

title: Organiser guide · Open the demo
text: From the developer console choose **Run full local demo**, then open [http://localhost:5173](http://localhost:5173). The demo signs you in as a tournament runner automatically. Use the account switcher in the navigation to see exactly what an official, club leader, fighter or spectator sees.

title: Organiser guide · Create your event in five steps
text: The setup wizard is at **Setup wizard** in the navigation. Your answers are saved as you go, so you can leave and come back without losing work.  1. **Event & identity** — name, dates, venue, logo, banner and colours. Choose a template if one looks similar to your event; everything in it can be changed. 2. **Disciplines & rules** — pick the contests you will run. Each one has match length, point v

title: Organiser guide · Invite clubs and register fighters
text: A club leader can register fighters under their club, upload a club logo and see only their own people. A fighter can register independently or accept a club invitation. Registration collects name, contact details, date of birth, height, weight, belt/grade and emergency information.  Enter metric or imperial measurements — whichever is easier. J3 stores the metric values and keeps what you typed f

title: Organiser guide · Let J3 build the draw
text: **Auto-run** in the readiness checklist creates balanced pools, seeds fighters by rank, spreads same-club fighters across different pools, adds BYEs where needed and assigns officials to mats. You can always drag a fighter to a different slot: J3 keeps a copy at every round so the full history remains visible.  If a pool is too small for elimination, J3 suggests round robin instead. For third plac

title: Organiser guide · Score a contest
text: Open the **Official console** on a tablet or laptop:  1. Select the contest and confirm you are assigned to it. Unassigned officials cannot score. 2. Start the clock. The referee can stop it; the scorekeeper resumes it on command. 3. Add techniques and penalties to the correct side. Moves appear on the scoreboard immediately and every change is attributed to you. 4. A submission or tap is an insta

title: Organiser guide · Kata and training
text: Kata competitions use a judge panel on phones or tablets. J3 drops the highest and lowest scores, averages the middle scores and applies the tie-break chain you configured. Rounds can be compulsory or chosen, include bunkai, and advance the top performers automatically. Weapon kata and training sessions are supported as well.

title: Organiser guide · Screens and displays
text: Every view has its own URL, so open each one in its own browser tab and drag it onto the projector, TV or LED wall:  | View | Use | |---|---| | `/public` | Public dashboard: next up, live results and event status | | `/display` | Full-screen scoreboard with fighter photos, clubs, officials and timers | | `/brackets` | Elimination and round-robin progression | | `/tables` | Standings, rankings, med

title: Organiser guide · Keep the event on track
text: The public clock and dashboard timeline show projected start and end times. If the day runs early or late, adjust the drift once and every projection updates. Rest warnings remind you when a fighter has another bout too soon, and the on-deck list shows who is next.

title: Organiser guide · Dealing with changes on the day
text: - **Withdrawal or no-show** — mark a forfeit with a reason; the pool rebalances and promotions adjust without deleting the original result. - **Injury** — record it as a technical outcome so ranking points stay consistent. - **Voluntary move up** — with the fighter's consent, place them in a heavier or older category. - **Too few entrants** — switch the affected category to round robin from the br

title: Organiser guide · Audit and exports
text: Every material action records who did it, when, what it affected and the before/after values. Runners and officials can filter the **Audit trail** to resolve disputes. **Data explorer** and the CSV buttons in **Check-in & import** export fights, entrants and standings. The full machine API is documented in the [API reference](/docs/api).

title: Organiser guide · Need help?
text: - [Developer guide](/docs/development) explains commands, architecture and troubleshooting. - [CI & releases](/docs/ci) explains the automated checks. - The TUI menu **Docs & guides** opens this site and refreshes the generated API reference.

title: Runner guide
text: The full event path: create, check in, score, publish and audit.

title: Runner guide · Runner guide
text: # Tournament runner guide  This is the complete path from an empty venue to published medals. Use the hands-on guide in the app if you want each step checked for you: **Guides & progress → Runner**.

title: Runner guide · Before you start
text: Have the event name, dates, venue, a logo or banner, a rough participant count and the names of your officials ready. You do not need to know federation rule numbers: J3 stores rules as reusable configuration.

title: Runner guide · 1. Create the event
text: Open **Setup wizard** and work through the five steps:  1. **Event** — name, display title, venue, dates and theme. 2. **Disciplines** — one row per discipline, with match length, rounds, scoring and kit requirements. 3. **Categories** — age, weight, height, grade and gender ranges. Set a participant cap. 4. **People** — paste invitations as `email, phone, role, club`. 5. **Review** — fix any red

title: Runner guide · 2. Check the draw
text: Open **Fight pools** and **Brackets**. Confirm that:  - pools are balanced and same-club fighters are spread; - BYEs are allocated to seeds where your format policy says so; - the third-place plan respects the "have they already met?" rule; - every category has enough entrants to be valid.  Use **Regenerate balanced pools** if the seed produced a poor spread. Manual drag/shuffle is available on th

title: Runner guide · 3. Brief your team
text: Open **Event config** and share it with officials and competitors. It lists required kit, match times, course attendance, venue information and the public schedule. Open **Display control** to assign dashboard templates to screens.

title: Runner guide · 4. Check-in and weigh-in
text: On **Check-in & import**, enter the official weight for each arrival. J3 flags anyone outside their declared class. Use **Add fighter** for late entries, and the CSV buttons to export start lists. Forfeits, no-shows and injuries are recorded from the same area so the draw can be rebalanced.

title: Runner guide · 5. Run the mats
text: On each **Mat control** console:  1. select a contest; 2. start the authoritative clock; 3. pause when the referee stops the bout; 4. log holds, penalties and techniques from **Official console**; 5. confirm the result, which locks the bout and publishes it everywhere.  Every confirmation asks for approval and writes an audit entry with actor, role, time and before/after values. See [live scoring

title: Runner guide · 6. Publish and celebrate
text: Open **Public board** on spectator screens, **Brackets** on the main wall and **Medal ceremony** for podium callouts. Use the PA controls to flash the next competitors and speak their names. **Tables & rankings** shows live club points and medals.

title: Runner guide · After the event
text: Use **Audit trail** to resolve disputes, **Data explorer** to query the allow-listed tables, and **Account admin** to remove or change access. Save the event as a template before the next tournament so categories, rules and branding are reused exactly.

title: Official guide
text: Assignments, corner scoring, penalties, clock and kata panels.

title: Official guide · Official guide
text: # Official & moderator guide  Your console is designed for one tap per action and confirmation before anything is committed. Use **Guides & progress → Officials** for a checked, hands-on run-through.

title: Official guide · Get assigned
text: A runner assigns officials to mats and contests. Sign in with your official account and open **Official console**. If you cannot see a contest, you are not assigned to it — ask the runner rather than trying to score from another account.

title: Official guide · Select the contest and corner
text: 1. Choose the contest in **Select contest**. 2. Tap **RED** or **BLUE** to choose the active corner. The button shows the fighter's name. 3. Search the technique palette by English name or romaji.  Points, penalties and submissions always apply to the active corner. Check the name before every entry.

title: Official guide · Log a technique
text: Tap a technique card, review the confirmation dialogue (technique, romaji and point value), then press **Confirm & log**. The score appears on the live scoreboard immediately. If you tapped the wrong corner or technique, use **Undo last entry** — the correction is audited.

title: Official guide · Penalties and cards
text: Penalty cards are in the same palette. A yellow card records a light foul; repeated fouls escalate according to the event's rule set. Red cards and disqualifications follow the configured penalty ladder. Never award a card without the confirmation step.

title: Official guide · Control the clock
text: The scorekeeper's **Mat control** is authoritative. Start the bout, pause for referee stoppages and resume on instruction. The public board mirrors this clock. Do not run a separate stopwatch as the source of truth.

title: Official guide · Submissions and instant wins
text: A submission overrides accumulated points. Use **Red submits** or **Blue submits** for an instant win; J3 records the tap and asks you to confirm the final result. See [scoring rules](/docs/scoring) for holds, golden score and tie-breaks.

title: Official guide · Kata panel judging
text: Switch to the **Kata panel** tab. Each performance has sections such as etiquette, demonstration and application, scored by each judge from 0–10. J3 drops the highest and lowest marks where the rule set requires it and publishes the authoritative total. Change a score and confirm; totals update on **Tables & rankings**.

title: Official guide · Finish the bout
text: Use **Red wins**, **Blue wins** or **Draw** in the Finish & override panel, then confirm. The result is locked, pushed to every display and written to the audit trail. If you need to correct it, ask a runner to use the recorded undo path.

title: Official guide · Handover
text: At the end of your assignment, check **Audit trail** for your actions and tell the runner about any incidents. Do not share your account with another official — assignments and audit entries must stay attributable.

title: Participant guide
text: Registration, profile, check-in and following your contests.

title: Participant guide · Participant guide
text: # Participant & spectator guide  Whether you are fighting, coaching or watching, J3 gives you a public view that never exposes private scoring drafts. Use **Guides & progress → Participants** for a checked tour of the main views.

title: Participant guide · Create your profile
text: On **Settings**, add your name, contact details, date of birth, height, weight, rank/grade and club. Enter metric or imperial units — the server converts and stores metric values as canonical. Belt colour is chosen from a colour block with a custom option for tenant-specific grades.

title: Participant guide · Register for the right division
text: Open the public sign-up page. J3 only offers categories you are compatible with based on age, weight, height and grade. Heavier or older divisions appear only if you explicitly consent to move up. Full categories are greyed out so you do not waste time applying.  Minors need guardian consent before registration is accepted.

title: Participant guide · Before the day
text: Read **Event config** for required kit, match length, venue, schedule, amenities and rest rules. Check the **Public board** for your next-up callout. Arrive in time for weigh-in; officials record your official weight and flag any out-of-class issue.

title: Participant guide · At the venue
text: - **Public board** — live contests, venue clock and "next up". - **Fight pools** — your group and scheduled opponents. - **Brackets** — progression through each round, including bronze decisions. - **Live scoreboard** — your contest with belt, club logo, moves and penalties. - **Tables & rankings** — standings, club points and medals.  If you are called to a mat, the announcer's toast flashes your

title: Participant guide · Results and appeals
text: Once a bout is confirmed, the result is locked. W/L/D always show a letter as well as a colour. If you believe a result is wrong, speak to the runner — corrections are made through a recorded audit path, not by editing the board directly.

title: Participant guide · Spectators
text: You do not need an account to watch public views. Open `/public`, `/brackets`, `/tables` and `/pools` in separate tabs or screens. Every view is URL-addressable and updates live.

title: Frequently asked questions
text: Offline use, categories, scoring, displays and recovery.

title: Frequently asked questions · Frequently asked questions
text: # Frequently asked questions

title: Frequently asked questions · Can I use J3 with no internet at the venue?
text: Yes. The venue server, database and web app all run on a local machine or LAN box. Phones and displays connect to it over Wi-Fi. Nothing in the normal scoring flow needs the cloud. A single SQLite file is the backup.

title: Frequently asked questions · Do I need to know federation rules?
text: No. Pick a template or accept the defaults. Every value — points, match length, penalties, categories, tie-break order, display layout — is editable in plain language before the event. Nothing is hard-coded per federation.

title: Frequently asked questions · Can one fighter enter more than one category?
text: That depends on your rule set. Some federations allow more than one age division, others allow one age and one weight. The compatibility policy is configured in the event, not fixed in the code.

title: Frequently asked questions · What happens if a category has only two entrants?
text: J3 selects an appropriate format from your policy. Two entrants can use best of three, three use a round robin, and small or uneven pools fall back to round robin rather than producing a broken bracket.

title: Frequently asked questions · How are same-club meetings avoided?
text: Seeding uses controlled randomisation with a same-club separation constraint. You can override a placement by dragging a fighter; the move is recorded in the audit trail.

title: Frequently asked questions · Who can change a score?
text: Only an official assigned to that contest, with a role that has the `fights` capability. The scorekeeper controls the board, the referee controls the clock, and a runner can override a locked result. Every change records the actor, timestamp and before/after values.

title: Frequently asked questions · How do I put different views on different screens?
text: Each view has its own URL. Open it in a new tab, then drag that tab onto the second monitor or full-screen it. Use **View builder** to compose a saved layout from live widgets, then assign that template to a screen in **Display control**.

title: Frequently asked questions · Which languages are supported?
text: The shared label dictionary includes English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, Punjabi, Arabic, Japanese, Korean and Mandarin. Appearance follows the system by default and can be overridden per user.

title: Frequently asked questions · Can I restore a tournament after a crash?
text: Yes. SQLite runs in WAL mode and the venue file can be backed up or restored mid-event. Results are committed as they are confirmed, so a restart continues from the last committed state.

title: Frequently asked questions · Where do I find the raw API contract?
text: Use the [API reference](/docs/api), the raw [OpenAPI file](/openapi.yaml) or the [API guide](/docs/api-guide).

title: Formats & promotion
text: Pools, BYEs, eliminations, bronze rules and history.

title: Formats & promotion · Formats & promotion
text: # Formats, pools & promotion  Format choice is a policy, not a hard-coded rule. J3 selects a format from the actual number of entrants and the event's constraints, then lets a moderator override it.

title: Formats & promotion · Selecting a format
text: | Entrants | Common J3 policy | |---|---| | 1 | No contest; single winner with its own ranking points | | 2 | Best of three, stop at 2–0 | | 3 | Round robin | | 4 | Round robin or single elimination with third-place match | | 5 | Round robin pool of five | | 6 | Two pools of three, top two cross to semis | | 7+ | Double elimination, repechage or multi-stage | | 9+/17+ | Single elimination until la

title: Formats & promotion · Round robin
text: The circle method generates every pairing once. Odd fields receive a BYE without duplicating fixtures. Standings use the configured tie-break chain, not just wins.

title: Formats & promotion · Pools
text: Automated pool generation balances pool sizes, seeds by rank and stats, and uses controlled randomisation to spread clubs. Organisers set the target pool size, maximum pools and separation rules. **Regenerate balanced pools** gives a different controlled seed; moderators can drag fighters between slots.

title: Formats & promotion · Elimination brackets
text: J3 supports single elimination, true double elimination (lower winner can win gold via a reset) and consolation double (lower winner can only win bronze). The distinction is stored in the format policy so it is never ambiguous.  BYEs are allocated by seed or title. First-round club or country separation avoids early same-club meetings where the policy allows it.

title: Formats & promotion · Third place and bronze
text: If the two losing semi-finalists have already met, J3 awards two bronze medals instead of scheduling a repeat. If they have not met, a third-place match is generated. This rule is configurable per discipline.

title: Formats & promotion · Promotion and history
text: Winners, losers and draws advance according to the rule set. Each round keeps a copy of the fighter card, so the bracket shows the full path. Rematches are avoided where configured. Forfeits and no-shows rebalance the affected pool and promotion path.

title: Formats & promotion · See also
text: - [Live scoring rules](/docs/scoring) - [Runner guide](/docs/runner) - [Tournament formats in the organiser guide](/docs/guide)

title: Live scoring rules
text: Points, holds, submissions, penalties and tie-breaks.

title: Live scoring rules · Live scoring rules
text: # Live scoring rules  J3 does not hard-code one federation's rules. The values below are the defaults shipped in the generic rule set; a runner can change every one in the setup wizard.

title: Live scoring rules · Score events
text: A score event has an actor, timestamp, corner, technique, point value and audit entry. Confirmed events are committed to SQLite immediately; every visualisation reads that committed data.  Common scoring families:  | Family | Typical values | |---|---| | Ippon / Waza-ari | Ippon 3, Waza-ari 1, Shido penalty; Ippon ends the contest | | BJJ points | takedown 2, sweep 2, guard pass 3, mount/back 4, a

title: Live scoring rules · Holds and submissions
text: A hold timer counts down live on the scoreboard. Reaching the configured threshold awards the configured score. A tap or verbal submission is an instant win that negates prior points and triggers promotion. Both paths require confirmation.

title: Live scoring rules · Penalties
text: Penalties use a configurable ladder:  - **yellow card** — light foul, may award an opponent point; - **red card** — serious foul or two light fouls; - **shido** — three accumulate to hansoku-make (disqualification); - **forfeit / injury / no-show** — recorded with a reason and consistent advancement rules.  Penalty badges appear on the offending fighter's side of the scoreboard, never only as a co

title: Live scoring rules · Clock and stoppages
text: The venue server owns the clock. The scorekeeper starts, pauses, resumes and submits results. Paused time is visually distinct so spectators can see a referee stoppage. Golden score or overtime is a separate configured phase with its own first-point rule.

title: Live scoring rules · Best-of-N and multi-round bouts
text: A bout can be a single contest, best of three or best of five. J3 tracks each round separately, then applies the configured series rule. The bracket keeps a copy of every fighter at each round so the full history remains visible.

title: Live scoring rules · Tie-breakers
text: Runners choose an ordered chain, for example: wins → submissions → points in winning bouts → head-to-head → fewest points conceded → fastest submission → positive play majority. The first rule that separates fighters decides the rank.

title: Live scoring rules · Result codes
text: Configurable outcome icons include WP/LP/DP (points), WS/LS (submission), WT/LT (technical/forfeit/DQ) plus yellow/red card badges. A result icon is always paired with text.

title: Live scoring rules · Confirmation and undo
text: No score, card or result becomes authoritative until confirmed. Undo is available per entry, attributed to the actor and visible in the audit trail. Results are locked after confirmation; corrections need an explicit, recorded path.

title: Displays & screens
text: Multi-screen routes, themes, PA and custom views.

title: Displays & screens · Displays & screens
text: # Displays & multi-screen views  Every view is a normal URL, so you can open as many as you need on separate TVs, projectors, tablets and phones. They all poll or stream committed server data and stay live.

title: Displays & screens · Core routes
text: | Route | Use | |---|---| | `/public` | Spectator dashboard, clock, next-up and live results | | `/display` | Main full-screen scoreboard | | `/mat` | Scorekeeper and timekeeper console | | `/brackets` | Progression, results and history | | `/tables` | Standings, kata, medals and club points | | `/pools` | All matchups and current status | | `/control` | Assign dashboard templates to screens and t

title: Displays & screens · What the scoreboard shows
text: The board includes the event title, mat number, banner and logo, both fighters with large avatars, belt designation, height/weight, club logo, corner colours, active referee and judges, recent moves with points, penalties on the correct side, and the authoritative clock. W/L/D always show a glyph as well as colour.

title: Displays & screens · Responsive layouts
text: Layouts adapt from a 6-inch phone to an ultrawide LED wall. On narrow screens, fighter cards stack vertically and the card slides into a bottom sheet. Ultrawide screens use the full available width rather than a centred column. Avatar areas stay large enough to read across a hall.

title: Displays & screens · Themes and branding
text: Themes are CSS custom properties plus uploaded assets: logo, banner, colours and fonts. The Street Fighter theme adds lineups, matchups and announcer energy. Club colours extracted from uploaded logos appear on cards, tables and brackets.

title: Displays & screens · PA and announcements
text: Use **Display control** or the announce button on Event config to trigger timed toasts, flash the next competitor's card and speak text with browser TTS. Multilingual labels are available for eleven locales.

title: Displays & screens · Custom views
text: **View builder** lets an authorised user drag live widgets onto a canvas, resize them, save/clone/delete named layouts and open one as its own URL. Combine clock, next-up, scoreboard, standings and medal widgets for a dedicated stat screen.

title: Displays & screens · Broadcast
text: `/overlay` provides a transparent HTML layer for OBS or vMix with a scorebug and lower thirds. Async network video replay remains a future enhancement.

title: Developer guide
text: Architecture, commands, contracts and troubleshooting.

title: Developer guide · Developer guide
text: # Developer guide  J3 is one Go binary (the venue server) plus one SvelteKit app (every screen). The binary owns SQLite and all authoritative state; the web app is a set of URL-addressable views that read and write through the API. No separate state is kept in displays.

title: Developer guide · Stack
text: | Layer | Choice | Why | |---|---|---| | Server | Go 1.27, `modernc.org/sqlite` | Single portable binary, no CGO, one-file backup | | API | REST + SSE, OpenAPI 3.1 in `api/openapi.yaml` | Shared contract and generated TypeScript types | | Web | SvelteKit + TypeScript + Bun | One app, many display modes | | Mobile | Capacitor (Android/iOS) + PWA | Judge phones and tablets use the same UI | | Tests

title: Developer guide · First run
text: ```bash bun run dev          # interactive TUI: demo, QA, builds, mobile, docs bun run demo         # non-interactive: seeded venue server + UI at :5173 bun run demo:full    # same, with a complete tournament (pools, fights, kata, medals) ```  Prefer `bun run dev` for exploration. The TUI has nested menus: arrow keys move, Enter selects, `q`/Esc goes back, and number keys jump directly to an item.

title: Developer guide · Project layout
text: ```text api/openapi.yaml          Single source of truth for the HTTP contract cmd/j3d                   Venue server entry point internal/api              Routes, middleware, RBAC guards, SSE hub internal/auth             Sessions, bcrypt/MFA, rate limits internal/config           Tenant config snapshots and themes internal/db               SQLite migrations and queries internal/rules

title: Developer guide · API and generated types
text: Change the contract in `api/openapi.yaml`, then run:  ```bash bun run generate:types ```  This writes `web/src/lib/api-types.d.ts`, which is committed. CI regenerates it and fails if the checked-in file is stale. A Go test also checks that every registered route appears in the spec.  The docs site reads a generated index at `web/static/docs/operations.json`. Regenerate the reference, search index

title: Developer guide · Adding a screen
text: 1. Create `web/src/routes/<name>/+page.svelte`. Use existing `app.css` tokens rather than raw colours so white-label themes still work. 2. If the screen is role-restricted, add it to `NAV_ITEMS` in `web/src/lib/nav.ts`. Public and docs routes are allow-listed in the root layout guard. 3. Read data through `web/src/lib/api.ts`, never from a separate store. Displays must reflect the committed databa

title: Developer guide · Live scoring rules
text: The server owns the clock and assigns a global order to committed events. Judge devices send idempotent mutations; a scorer must be assigned to the contest and hold the right role. Results lock after confirmation, undo is recorded, and SSE fans state out to every display. Do not add a client-side score buffer — it would break the audit trail.

Use a prefixed branch:  | Prefix | Purpose | |---|---| | `feature/` | new capability | | `bug/` | defect | | `fix/` | correction | | `chore/` | maintenance | | `perf/` | performance work | | `improv/` | UI/UX refinement | | `release/` | release preparation | | `hotfix/` | urgent production fix |  `develop` is optional integration bran

text: - **Android**: syncs Capacitor, builds a debug APK, uploads it as a workflow artifact. - **iOS**: builds an unsigned simulator `.app` on macOS and uploads a zip artifact. A device-installable IPA is produced automatically when the `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_P12`, `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_PROVISIONING_PROFILE`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID` and `APPLE_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_NAME` secrets are configured; otherw

title: CI & releases · Environments (.github/workflows/deploy.yml)
text: Manual `workflow_dispatch` deploys to `development`, `staging` and `production` in order, each behind a GitHub **environment** (configure required reviewers in repository settings). Set `DEPLOY_HOST*`, `DEPLOY_USER` and `DEPLOY_PATH*` secrets to enable rsync deployment; without a host the workflow validates the bundle locally.

title: CI & releases · Releases (.github/workflows/release.yml)
text: Triggered by pushing a `v*` tag (or manual dispatch). It re-runs CI, builds mobile artifacts, packages the Go binaries (Linux, macOS, Windows), copies the static web build, and publishes everything as a GitHub release with generated notes.

title: CLI & TUI · Build and deploy
text: The **Build** menu creates a release binary and can locally verify the CI/CD script. Deployment is environment-gated: staging and production require the matching environment variables and credentials. Release artifacts include the venue binary and mobile builds.

title: CLI & TUI · Mobile
text: The **Mobile** menu prepares Capacitor projects, builds an Android APK and launches an Android Studio emulator. On this host the reliable emulator command uses `~/Android/Sdk`, the `j3-pixel-10-pro` AVD and `-gpu auto`. iOS builds require macOS and Xcode.

title: CLI & TUI · Data and reset
text: Use **Reset demo data** to restore the seeded tournament. The full seed includes 40 fighters, four clubs, kata scores, medals, pools, brackets and an audit trail. A single SQLite file is the portable backup.

title: CLI & TUI · Troubleshooting
text: If the docs site shows a proxy error, confirm the API is listening on `127.0.0.1:8787` and that the Vite proxy regex forwards `^/api/`. If a page shows stale data after a reset, reload once — the client automatically retries with a fresh demo session after a 401.

title: API guide · Errors
text: `400` validation, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not found, `409` conflict, `500` generic with the details logged against the request ID. Raw database errors are never returned to clients.
